_comment: Input to L0-solution-architect at Cycle 0, HarvestLink marketplace. The target architecture is a Confluence page; here a copy is supplied directly as target_architecture_output (shown as L0-design-target-architect's examples/output-01 with the Enterprise Architect's approval applied), which takes precedence over fetching the page, so no reader call is made for it. At runtime without a direct copy, tool-L0-confluence-reader returns the page in storage-format XHTML. prd_page_id is empty: the target carries every budget used. Technology approval comes from kb-L0-enterprise-architecture EA11, not an input file.

bounded_contexts.name: Catalogue
bounded_contexts.rationale_summary: Listing lifecycle is editorial and runs on the producer's clock. Merged with Orders, every listing edit would release the checkout path and order state would leak into a producer-owned model.

bounded_contexts.name: Orders
does_not_own: Listing price (Catalogue — captured at placement only)
bounded_contexts.rationale_summary: The order lifecycle is operational and changes weekly under Product; fee policy changes quarterly under Finance and fee records are tax records. Merged with Billing, every fee change redeploys checkout and financial records inherit operational retention.

bounded_contexts.name: Billing
does_not_own: Tax policy beyond one rate card (OPEN-02)
bounded_contexts.rationale_summary: Fee calculation is commercial policy under Finance approval and fee records fall under 10-year tax retention. Payouts stay here because they derive from Billing's transactions under the same regulator; splitting them creates a second financial system of record.

bounded_contexts.name: Identity
does_not_own: Whether a listing may be published (Catalogue)
Group wholesale supplier records (group supplier master)
bounded_contexts.rationale_summary: FBO registration is a regulated fact about the producer with a validity window, needed by both Catalogue and Orders, so it sits upstream of both. Merged with Catalogue, Orders would depend on Catalogue for a regulated identity fact.

bounded_contexts.name: Notifications
bounded_contexts.rationale_summary: Stateless: delivery must be retryable and replaceable without touching a source of truth, and a context with no entities cannot drift. Merged into Orders, Billing's payout events would flow through Orders.

interaction_edges.purpose: Availability and current price of the listings in a basket
Notice that an order was placed, with lines and amounts

Who the caller is and what they may do

invariants.rule: A Listing may not be published while its producer's FBO registration is not valid; the check is repeated at checkout
invariants.violation_looks_like: A buyer completes an order for a producer whose registration had expired

invariants.rule: A Listing price is a positive, exact amount in the smallest currency unit; it is never rounded
invariants.violation_looks_like: A listing with a zero, negative or fractional-penny price exists

invariants.rule: An Order captures each line's price at placement and is never re-priced; the buyer pays what they saw
invariants.violation_looks_like: An order total differs from the confirmation the buyer received

invariants.rule: Submitting the same order request twice yields one Order
invariants.violation_looks_like: Two orders exist for one buyer request

invariants.rule: A Fee has no life independent of the Transaction that produced it
invariants.violation_looks_like: A fee exists with no transaction

invariants.rule: A Fee is immutable once written; corrections are new compensating entries, never updates
invariants.violation_looks_like: An auditor finds a fee whose value changed after it was written

invariants.rule: A Payout includes each settled Transaction of its producer and period exactly once
invariants.violation_looks_like: A transaction is paid out twice, or a settled transaction is never paid out

invariants.rule: A Producer's FBO registration validity windows are kept as history; a window is never overwritten
invariants.violation_looks_like: Validity at a past date cannot be reconstructed

constraints.rule: Every bounded context is realised by at least one independently deployable component; no component spans two contexts
constraints.rationale_summary: Independent deployability makes a boundary real (PRIN-04).
constraints.observable_violation: A component writing entities owned by two contexts

constraints.rule: Exactly one system of record per entity
constraints.rationale_summary: Two sources of truth leave no correct value to restore (PRIN-02).

constraints.rule: Non-owning contexts hold references by identifier only; a replicated attribute only in a registered read model with a staleness budget
constraints.rationale_summary: Unregistered copies become second systems of record (PRIN-02).
constraints.observable_violation: A field mirroring another context's attribute with no registration

constraints.rule: No context reads or writes another context's persistent state directly
constraints.rationale_summary: Direct reads couple contexts at the storage level (PRIN-03).
constraints.observable_violation: A cross-context query or shared store

constraints.rule: Every cross-context interaction is asynchronous unless a REQ-INT demand states a synchronous need with a latency budget and a degraded-mode behaviour
constraints.observable_violation: A synchronous cross-context call with no matching REQ-INT budget

constraints.rule: All inter-context communication uses a published, versioned contract
constraints.observable_violation: A consumer relying on an undocumented interface

constraints.rule: A value displayed by one context but owned by another is obtained through that context's contract, never inferred or recomputed
constraints.rationale_summary: A recomputed value drifts from the owner's rule (FR-006).
constraints.observable_violation: Two contexts producing different values for the same business fact

constraints.rule: Identity is upstream of every context; no context implements its own authentication
constraints.rationale_summary: One authority on who a caller is (ES1).
constraints.observable_violation: A component that authenticates users itself

constraints.rule: A context may hold a transactional snapshot of another context's value only as part of an immutable record of an event: captured once through the owner's contract, declared, never reconciled
constraints.rationale_summary: Physically identical to a replicated attribute, semantically opposite; without the rule a snapshot gets 'fixed' and INV-03 breaks.
constraints.observable_violation: An undeclared copy, or a declared snapshot being synchronised

constraints.rule: Every entity classified PII, Financial or Regulated Evidence carries a retention and residency policy before it is first persisted
constraints.rationale_summary: Retention decided after data exists is decided under pressure (PRIN-06).
constraints.observable_violation: A classified entity persisted with no retention or residency decision

constraints.rule: No context posts to an enterprise financial ledger; the platform's financial records are held only in Billing
constraints.rationale_summary: HarvestLink is not a transacting party in the group ledger (EA3).
constraints.observable_violation: Any interface from a HarvestLink component to the group ledger

constraints.rule: Any deviation from a binding principle is recorded with a rationale, or it is a defect
constraints.rationale_summary: An unrecorded deviation cannot be reviewed or reversed.
constraints.observable_violation: A design that breaks a principle with no DEV or EXC record

demands.budget: Every cross-context event; no consumer broken by a producer version change

demands.demand: The producer's FBO validity at publication and at checkout

demands.demand: Notice of order placed and payout scheduled

demands.demand: Every value obtained through the owning service's contract

demands.demand: Settlement status of each transaction from the external payment provider
demands.budget: At-least-once; all settlements for a period received before its close

demands.demand: Whether a registering producer already exists as a group supplier
demands.budget: Read-only (EA3); latency and failure behaviour PENDING
demands.viewpoint_decides: Access route to the group supplier master

demands.demand: Every integration observable by correlation id, trace id and contract version
demands.budget: 100% of APP-2.3 edges

demands.demand: Independently deployable runtime, one deployment unit per APP-2 component
demands.budget: No component redeploys another; checkout path 99.9% monthly

demands.demand: Durable asynchronous messaging with replay
demands.budget: At-least-once; replay window >= 24 h

demands.demand: Long-term immutable retention tier suitable for tax audit

demands.viewpoint_decides: Storage tier; how the guarantee is evidenced

demands.demand: Large binary object storage and delivery

demands.demand: Scheduled, non-interactive job execution

demands.demand: Evidenced outbound email delivery

demands.demand: Central logging, metrics, tracing and alerting for every workload

demands.demand: Text search over published listings
Group-approved external-party identity capability

demands.demand: Managed key and secret capability with per-component workload identity
demands.budget: Rotation without redeploying unrelated components; zero shared credentials

open_structural_decisions.decision: Whether an analytical plane exists, and which context owns it
open_structural_decisions.why_not_now: No committed requirement aggregates across time or contexts

trigger_clauses: aggregates over more than one month of history
joins data across two bounded contexts
options_in_view: Two-plane model with a registered analytical read model owned by one context
open_structural_decisions.owner_when_fired: Solution Architect; Enterprise Architect if a CON is amended

open_structural_decisions.decision: Whether tax rules and their effective dates become a bounded context

a tax-authority-facing document (invoice, return) is required
options_in_view: Extend Billing's rate card only if none of (a)-(c) hold

open_structural_decisions.decision: Whether Notifications stays stateless or gains entities
open_structural_decisions.why_not_now: No requirement for per-recipient preferences or history

trigger_clauses: per-recipient delivery preferences must be stored
a recipient must query their delivery history

deviations.why_summary: Availability, fee and FBO validity are checked or shown in the buyer's request path, where staleness is visible and disputable.
deviations.accepted_cost: Orders depends at runtime on Catalogue, Billing and Identity; Catalogue on Identity
deviations.review_trigger: Confirmation-time fee changes become impossible by policy

collisions.resolution_summary: Introduce the transactional snapshot: captured once through Catalogue's contract at placement, declared, never reconciled.
collisions.resulting_change: CON-09 added; CON-03 exception names it; REQ-DAT-08 added

collisions.resolution_summary: PREC-02: a stated request-path budget with degraded-mode behaviour prevails over the async default.

options_rejected.rejected: Orders computes and stores the fee
options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: Couples Finance-approved policy to the order lifecycle; fee records would inherit Orders' retention instead of 10-year tax retention.
options_rejected.reopen_condition: Fee fixed by law rather than commercial decision

options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: A fact about the producer that Orders must also check; two consumers put it upstream of both.

options_rejected.rejected: Three (Notifications in Orders; Identity as shared kernel)
options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: A shared kernel couples every context to one schema; Notifications in Orders routes Billing events through Orders.
options_rejected.reopen_condition: OPEN-03 never fires and event volume stays trivial

options_rejected.chosen: Build Identity over a group-approved external identity capability
options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: Group identity is employees-only and must not be extended to external parties (EA2, ES1).
options_rejected.reopen_condition: The group launches an external-party identity tier

options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: An access pattern over Catalogue data with no language of its own.
options_rejected.reopen_condition: Ranking becomes a business policy with its own owner

options_rejected.why_rejected_summary: Derived from Billing's transactions under the same regulator; splitting creates a second financial system of record.
options_rejected.reopen_condition: Payouts across several payment rails with their own regimes
A single persona routinely needs both roles

adr_seeds.decision_summary: Fees never updated; corrections are compensating entries

adr_seeds.title: Transactional snapshots
adr_seeds.decision_summary: Snapshots declared, captured once, never reconciled

assumptions.assumption: Card capture and settlement are done by an external regulated provider

artifacts.description: HarvestLink target architecture v1.0, APPROVED by the Enterprise Architect 2026-10-22. Full text: L0-design-target-architect/examples/artifacts/target-architecture.md (status line reads DRAFT there; approved copy is identical apart from front matter).

content.execution_summary:
• Produced target-architecture.md v1.0 (DRAFT, gate_ready: true): 5 contexts, 8 components, 10 edges, 10 aggregates, 8 invariants, 12 constraints, 30 demands (8 DAT, 12 INT, 10 PLT), 7 controls, 3 OPEN triggers.
• Non-obvious boundaries: FBO registration in Identity rather than Catalogue (different regulator; two consumers); Payouts kept in Billing (same regulator; splitting creates a second financial SoR); Search kept inside Catalogue (no language of its own).
• Collisions: INV-03 (order keeps price shown) vs CON-03/CON-07 (identifier only) — resolved by CON-09 transactional snapshot, ADR-006 proposed. Request-path needs vs async default — DEV-01 under PREC-02.
• PENDING budgets: REQ-INT-05 identity latency (OQ-01); REQ-INT-11 supplier-master latency and failure behaviour (OQ-02).
• Principles: PROVISIONAL from the kb-L0-enterprise-architecture catalogue — binding-principles.json absent. DEV-01 against PRIN-03 (DIRECTIONAL).
• KBs: kb-L0-enterprise-architecture — PRIN-01..08 hooks, PREC-02, EA2/EA3 (employee-only group identity, no ledger posting, read-only supplier master). kb-L0-enterprise-security — ES1 external identity, ES2 classes, ES3 6-year regulated evidence, ES9 residency, ES10 encryption and attribution.
• Guardrails: gr-L0-output-schema-validator pass; gr-L0-hallucination-check pass; gr-L0-consistency-check pass; gr-L0-pii-detection pass.
• Tools: tool-L0-azure-blob-reader (1 call; prd.md found, binding-principles.json and vision.md absent); tool-L0-azure-blob-writer wrote s3://adlc-artifacts/harvestlink/wf-hl-step1-4b7e21c9/target-architecture.md.
